You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The policy rate is high relative to its 3-year average (+1.5) but fell sharply over 3 months (-2.0), which points to the start of a cutting cycle. The dollar is strong (+1.5, +2.0 over 12m). Headline CPI is low (-1.0). Unemployment is low relative to its average but rising. VIX fell sharply over 3 months, so a spike has just faded. Equities rallied over 3 months after a weak 6 months.

Candidate: late 2019. The Fed cut in Jul, Sep and Oct 2019, but the 3-year policy rate z-score would be about +1 there. The dollar was strong in 2019. However, 10y yields fell over 12m and the 10y-2y spread was flat. Industrial production was weak in 2019, and a VIX drop over 3m fits Dec 2019 versus Aug 2019. Credit spread +1.5 over 12m also fits, since Dec 2018 had wide spreads, but that would be lower by Dec 2019. The 6m equity return of -1.5 doesn't fit 2019.

Candidate: early 2025 or late 2025. The Fed cut in Sep-Dec 2024 and again in late 2025. In early 2025, 12m equity returns were strong, so that doesn't fit.

Candidate: late 2007/early 2008. The Fed cut from Sep 2007. The window is only the last 36 months, though, and the data begin in 2007, so z-scores before 2010 would be hard to compute. That makes it unlikely.

Candidate: mid-2020? Not consistent with a policy rate at +1.5.

Candidate: Dec 2025/Jan 2026? Policy rate cuts of -2.0 over 3m seem too large.

Candidate: Dec 2008 or early 2009? The 12m equity return would be very negative, so no.

Candidate: Jan 2016? The Fed was hiking then, so no.

Candidate: Nov 2024? Equity 12m would be strongly positive, so no.

Candidate: Oct 2019 to Jan 2020. Headline CPI at -1.0 with core at 0 fits. Equity 6m at -1.5 doesn't fit, but the z-scores of returns versus the last 36 months may be odd, since 2017-2018 had strong and steady returns. The vol 6m of +2.0 is high, though. This could instead be 2019 Jan-Feb, but the policy rate was still rising then.

Alternative: the 2020 Fed cut. Feb 2020 had a rate z around +1.5 and the dollar was strong. But the VIX would be high then.

Alternative: late 2019 with the Treasury 1m return of +1.5 to +2.0? Treasuries rallied in Aug 2019, and the VIX was up then. In Oct 2019, Treasuries fell. So a month in which Treasuries rose, equities were flat, and the VIX fell over 3 months fits poorly with late 2019.

Alternative: Sep-Oct 2024? VIX was down, but 12m equity was strongly positive.

Alternative: mid-2007 to early 2008. A policy rate that is high versus its 2004-07 history and fell 2.0 over 3m fits Jan 2008. But the VIX would be up.

I'll go with Dec 2019.
